state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To find the net of a three-dimensional shape, it's important to visualize how the flat shape will fold to form the 3D shape. In this case, the net of a circle touching a sector would actually form a cone when folded. Remember to consider how the shapes connect and fold together when determining the net of a 3D shape.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the circle and the sector fold together to make a cone? I think I see it now - like the sector wraps around and the circle becomes the base... but I'm still a bit confused about how they actually connect when you fold it up. Does the curved edge of the sector have to match the edge of the circle or something?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When folding the net of a cone, the curved edge of the sector should match up with the edge of the circle to form the cone shape. Visualize the sector wrapping around the circle to create the cone structure. Keep practicing visualizing how the shapes connect and fold together to better understand the net of a 3D shape.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher correctly identifies the shape as a cone and addresses the visualization challenge, but primarily tells rather than guides discovery, and while the student shows some progress in understanding, they remain somewhat confused about the connection mechanism by the end.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides some direct instruction about how the shapes connect and gives corrective feedback that it forms a cone rather than a triangle, but lacks explicit step-by-step procedures or worked examples that would characterize a strong rule-based approach.
